channel.title: Pier & Point · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement (Pier 70), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: The 22nd Street Caltrain accessibility project's schedule and total cost came from an SFCTA board packet that could not be re-read. The record now follows SFCTA's own April 2026 post: design funded and expected to finish by summer 2027, with construction funding sought to finish the project by June 2029. The $19.1 million total is still listed but marked as not re-checked.

item.title: Milestone · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: The Federal Transit Administration's All Stations Accessibility Program awards the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board $14.1 million for ADA improvements at the 22nd Street station -- matching almost exactly the funding gap SFCTA's own April 2026 plan had left as "Planned TBD". (Sep 10, 2026)

item.title: Milestone · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: SFCTA Board formally approves the $1,300,000 Prop L design-phase allocation (one of three projects sharing a combined $9.8M Prop L allocation that day, alongside the Powell St Improvement and the Mission Bay Ferry Landing). (Apr 28, 2026)

item.title: Expected · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: Caltrain is seeking construction funding to implement the project by June 2029 (SFCTA, April 28, 2026); construction was not yet funded then, so this is a target, not a schedule. (~2029)

item.title: Milestone · 22nd St Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement: SFCTA's Transportation Authority Board packet recommends $1,300,000 in Prop L funds for the project's design phase, part of a total funding plan of $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design). The packet could not be re-read in October 2026 (it refuses automated fetches); the $1,300,000 design request is confirmed by SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post, the total and breakdown are not re-checked. (Apr 14, 2026)
